name: ship
description:
SHIP is your autonomous software team. Assign a Linear, Jira or GitHub issue to SHIP, and its autonomous coding agents plan, build, review and test the change in your own GitHub repository. A mission works toward a pull request. Your CI, an automated code review and a test of its acceptance criteria each gate it.

Hand work to SHIP from the assistant you already use. File a mission from an issue in your tracker, or from a title and a description. Follow the mission through its stages, and read its verdicts, cost and session logs. Send an instruction to the agent that runs next, or leave a note for it. Read the proof that a run produced, such as test traces and screenshots.

SHIP runs agentic development as a headless AI software factory, so no screen has to be in the loop. You operate the whole mission from your coding agent, your AI assistant, your tracker or your terminal. A Planner, a Builder, a Reviewer and a Tester each do one stage of the agentic SDLC. They follow the agentic engineering practices in your repository, such as its agent instructions and skills. Your CI and a preview deploy are gates between the roles, and work that fails a gate goes back to the Builder with the reason.

Schedule maintenance missions, such as a weekly dependency upgrade. Manage the preview environments of your pull requests and the MCP servers that your agents use.

Sign in with OAuth, or send a SHIP personal access token. A token that you bind to one project can reach only the missions of that project.

You need a SHIP account and a connected GitHub repository. Create an account at https://letsship.ai.

capabilities: File a mission from an issue or a description
Follow a mission through plan, build, review and test
Send instructions to the agent that runs next
Read test traces, screenshots and session logs
defaultPrompt: Which SHIP projects can you reach, and what stage is each open mission in?
Assign SHIP-412 to SHIP. Tell me when its pull request passes CI, review and tests.
Turn the plan we just wrote into a SHIP mission that starts at the Builder.

positive.description: List the projects that the token can reach.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the demo project with its repository name.

positive.description: File a new mission from a description, with acceptance criteria.
positive.prompt: File a SHIP mission in the demo project to fix the typo on the pricing page.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates an issue and a mission, and returns the issue id and its link.

positive.description: Read the state of a mission.
positive.prompt: What stage is the last mission in, and what did the Reviewer say?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the current stage and the latest review verdict of the mission.

positive.description: Send review feedback to the agent that runs next.
positive.prompt: Tell the Builder on that mission to keep the old route and add the new one beside it.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns a receipt that says what SHIP recorded and what the instruction will start.

positive.description: Read the proof that a QA run produced.
positive.prompt: Show the proof from the last QA run.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the test trace and screenshots of the run, each with a link.

negative.description: A travel request has nothing to do with SHIP.
SHIP has no tool that deletes a repository.
A weather question has nothing to do with SHIP.
